html:
Arawakan, also called Maipurean, is a family of Indigenous languages of South America, the Caribbean and Central America. Before 1492 it was the most widespread language family in the Americas, spoken from the Bahamas to Bolivia and from the Andes foothills to the mouth of the Amazon.

Its speakers were mostly river farmers who grew manioc and spread along the rivers of Amazonia; from the Orinoco they moved into the Caribbean islands from about 500 BCE.

Some of its best known peoples:

  • The Taíno of the Greater Antilles, the first people Columbus met in 1492. English words such as "hammock", "canoe" and "hurricane" come from their language.
  • The Lokono of the Guianas, the original "Arawaks".
  • The Kalinago of the Lesser Antilles, who spoke an Arawakan language despite being called Caribs.
  • The Asháninka, the Nanti and other Kampa peoples of Peru, the Yine, the Baure of Bolivia, and the Wayuu of Colombia and Venezuela, today the largest Arawakan-speaking people.

Many of these languages now have few speakers. Its neighbours in Amazonia include the Tupian and Cariban families.
